issues.location: subterm relation example for the literal letters a and b
issues.finding: One inline subterm expression prints bare italic b while all adjacent occurrences denote the literal letter with \mathrm{b}. The switch is inconsistent within the same case analysis.
issues.proposed_resolution: Write \mathrm{b} as the second argument in that subterm expression.

issues.location: second decomposition of the bracketless a-b-c-d string
issues.finding: The first factor of the second decomposition prints bare italic b, while the whole string and all other letters in the displayed decomposition use \mathrm for literal symbols.
issues.proposed_resolution: Write \mathrm{b} in the first factor r_1.

translation_treatment: The Javanese target uses the literal-letter macro for b in both places. A bounded comparison view records the corrections; the frozen English bytes remain unchanged.
